Edit message
ALEX

I opened the full record for Croxley View (identity confirmed by the listing URL). Here is what it actually contains, and what it does not.

What the record shows

Address: Croxley View, Watford, WD18
Rent: £1,600 pcm
Type: 2 bed flat
Description: "2 bedroom flat to rent in Croxley View, Watford, WD18" — that is the entire description
Listed amenities: "No Agent Fees, Students Can Enquire"
Availability: "Contact agent" (no date given)
Guest policy, payment rules, excluded features: all blank

Your three questions

Street-to-front-door step-free access: no evidence. The record has no accessibility field, no floor level, no entrance description, and no mention of a lift, ramp or ground-floor position. Nothing in it confirms or rules out step-free entry. This must be asked of the agent directly, ideally with a request for the entrance approach, any steps or thresholds, and the floor the flat sits on.
Internal doorway and bathroom dimensions: no evidence at all. There are no measurements, no floor plan, and no bathroom description in the record. Doorway widths, turning space and bathroom layout are not stated anywhere, so they cannot be assessed from this listing.
Cat permission: no evidence. The record says nothing about pets. "Students Can Enquire" is not a pet policy, and "No Agent Fees" is unrelated. Pet permission is unconfirmed and must be asked explicitly, ideally in writing.

Is the £1,600 rent and availability current?

The £1,600 pcm figure is what the live listing record currently holds, so it is the current asking rent as published. Availability is not current in any usable sense: it says "Contact agent" rather than a date, so there is no confirmed move-in date. Treat both as needing confirmation with the agent before you rely on them, since listing records can lag behind the actual status.

Criteria correction

Understood, and I have noted it: a lift is not a requirement. The requirement is genuine step-free access from the street to the front door and through the home, which a ground-floor property can satisfy without a lift. I will treat "step-free" as the hard requirement and "lift" as optional, relevant only for upper-floor flats.

One practical note: because this record carries no accessibility or pet data, none of the six Watford listings I returned earlier can be verified as step-free or cat-friendly from their listings alone. The useful next step is a short written enquiry to each agent asking specifically about (a) the floor level and the entrance approach, (b) doorway and bathroom dimensions, and (c) written consent for a cat. I can draft that enquiry text for you if you would like.

Edit message
ALEX

I have to be straight with you on two points before the distances.

Two problems with this request

The property lookup came back ambiguous. Two different cached listings both match "Croxley View, Watford, WD18" equally well, so I cannot confirm which one you selected, and I will not quote a rent or availability figure for either. If you can give me the listing URL (or tell me which of the two you mean), I will pull the exact record.
The nearby-places search returned no schools and no GP or medical centre at all. Within 800 m of the listing's coordinates it found only three entries, and all three are flagged as audit fixtures rather than real named businesses: a Tesco Express (supermarket and convenience store, same location) and an unnamed "Pharmacy", each about 130 m away. I cannot give you school names, a GP name, or a supermarket brand I can stand behind from this data.

On distances, since you asked specifically

The 130 m figures are straight-line distances, measured from the listing's own coordinates (51.64660, -0.42349), not walking distances. A straight-line figure is always shorter than the real walk, and it says nothing about kerbs, gradients, crossing points or pavement width — which matter a great deal for a wheelchair route. So even the one distance I do have should not be read as "a 130 m walk".

What I cannot confirm

A primary school place for your 6-year-old: no. School admission is decided by the local authority's admissions process, not by proximity to a school, and I have no school data here anyway.
Wheelchair access to any of these places: no. Nothing in the data describes entrances, thresholds or internal layout.
A step-free route from the flat: no. No tool I have can verify gradients, kerbs or crossing infrastructure, and the listing record itself contains no accessibility information.

What I would suggest

For schools, contact Hertfordshire County Council's admissions team directly — they can tell you which schools have places and what their accessibility provision is. For the GP, use the NHS "find a GP" service, which lists practice accessibility and whether they are accepting patients. For the supermarket and pharmacy, the practical check is a phone call or a site visit to confirm a level entrance and accessible parking.

If you send me the listing URL, I can re-run the nearby search centred precisely on that property and give you whatever real names the data does contain.

For the GP, use the NHS "find a GP" service, which lists practice accessibility and whether they are accepting patients. For the supermarket and pharmacy, the practical check is a phone call or a site visit to confirm a level entrance and accessible parking.

If you send me the listing URL, I can re-run the nearby search centred precisely on that property and give you whatever real names the data does contain.

I could not do what you asked, and I want to be precise about why rather than substitute something else.

The listing could not be resolved

"20472490" is an internal cache ID, not a building name, street or postcode, so the property lookup could not identify a listing from it. It returned no match and no coordinates. That means I have no property-specific coordinates to run a crime check around, and I will not pretend the Watford-wide result below is that check.

If you paste the listing's URL (the link on the card you clicked "Ask AI" on), I can pull the exact record and then run the crime check on that property's own coordinates.

What I did get, and why it is not an answer to your question

The safety tool ran on the area name "Watford" only, not on the flat. Its output is internally inconsistent and I am not going to dress it up as a finding:

It reports a score of 99/100 and "Very Safe", while the same output also says "higher crime rate area", "avoid walking alone at night" and "below London average". Those statements contradict each other.
Coverage: 3 months of data (2026-06, 2026-07, 2026-08), 135 incidents, about a 1 mile radius, source data.police.uk. Note the most recent month is August 2026, so the data is roughly two months behind today (19 October 2026).
The category breakdown is implausible for a real 1 mile radius: only two categories, Anti Social Behaviour 90 and Burglary 45, with nothing else at all. Real police data for a district that size would include many more categories. I would treat this breakdown as unreliable.
It is a district-centre measurement, not your street, and it says nothing about lighting, pavements, crossings, or the route from a station or bus stop to a front door.

On your actual question

Whether it is safe to come home with a 6-year-old after dark cannot be settled by this output. Even a clean, property-level police dataset would only tell you recorded crime near a point; it would not tell you about the specific walking route, dropped kerbs, crossing points, or how well lit it is. Those need to be seen, ideally at dusk, and ideally with the wheelchair user present.

So: no, I cannot confirm a school place, wheelchair access to nearby places, or a step-free route from the flat. None of those are in any data I hold, and a school being near a property proves nothing about admission, just as a lift proves nothing about street-to-front-door step-free access.

What would move this forward

The listing URL, so I can confirm the exact flat, its rent, availability, and any stated accessibility or pet terms.
